items.question: What should I bring to my first neurosurgical consultation?
items.answer: Please bring your recent MRI or CT scan disc/digital link, radiology reports, a list of current medications, and any prior physical therapy or pain management notes.

items.question: Does a neurosurgical consultation always mean I will need surgery?
items.answer: No. Over half of the patients we evaluate are successfully managed with targeted physical therapy, image-guided injections, or structured observation without surgery.

items.question: How long is recovery after minimally invasive spine surgery?
items.answer: Most patients undergoing microdiscectomy or endoscopic decompression walk the same day and resume light daily activities within 1 to 2 weeks.

items.question: Do you offer second-opinion reviews for brain or spine surgery recommendations?
items.answer: Yes. Our board-certified neurosurgeons provide comprehensive second-opinion evaluations—either in-clinic or after reviewing your high-resolution imaging.

items.question: Do you accept major health insurance plans?
items.answer: Yes, we work with most major PPO and commercial medical insurance carriers and assist with pre-authorization for diagnostic imaging and surgical procedures.
